title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Yoga and Pilates
audience: Yoga and Pilates teachers and studio operators, including solo teachers, who want to charge more for courses, memberships, reformer classes or workplace classes.
learningOutcomes: Write a class offer with a measurable outcome you control, a time frame and clear conditions
Identify the joining, pausing and cancellation friction a student carries, and reduce it
Price the offer on value, then check it against your hours, costs and insurance

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'Drop-in yoga, $25' is a price for a class. 'A six-week beginner series: set class times, a written home practice plan, a check-in in week three, and a make-up class if I cancel one of your sessions' is an offer. The student buys a structured course and a clear promise about what happens if something goes wrong. Do not promise flexibility, strength, stress or health results. Promise the classes you will run, the plan you will give and the checks you will make.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: Name the outcome you control: the classes delivered, the written plan and the check-in. Set a time frame that matches the course or membership. Name the student's work, such as attending booked times and bringing the home plan to the next class. Give certainty through a published timetable, a written plan and clear rules for pausing or missing a class. State the risk you carry, such as a make-up class when you cancel, backed by the cover you hold. Put scope and exclusions in writing. A written quote can become binding once it is accepted, and exclusions should name what is outside the offer, such as private sessions, workshops or reformer classes (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Joining, pausing and no-lock-in wording
instruction.body: Studios compete on how easily a student can join and pause. Central Yoga's public terms list a two-week unlimited intro at $40, offered on first purchase only. The terms include a minimum of two debits, no fixed term, unused classes that are not lost, and memberships that can be paused (Central Yoga, undated). ASMY's Mermaid Beach timetable lists a one-month unlimited intro at $49, with no lock-in, bought once (ASMY, page modified 6 November 2026). These are two studios' own terms, not market rates. Be careful with 'no contracts' wording. The ACCC warned in 2014, as reported by the Consumers Federation, that the term is likely misleading where cancellation needs written notice, payments continue through a notice period, or a non-refundable upfront payment is required (Consumers Federation of Australia, 9 July 2014, an older report). Reformer Pilates needs the same clarity. The University of Wollongong's UniActive excludes reformer classes from its memberships and asks for cancellation at least six hours before a class to receive a credit (UOW UniActive, undated).

instruction.heading: Cancellation and prepayment rules by state
instruction.body: Western Australia's fitness code of practice covers yoga classes. It says cancellation by email is enough, that cancellation can take effect up to 30 days after notice, and that cancellation for illness needs a medical certificate. The page does not say whether the code is mandatory (WA Consumer Protection, published and updated 2 April 2025). Queensland says prepayment may not run more than 12 months ahead, and that prepaid money is refunded within 14 days, less services used and any disclosed admin fee. Its scope is 'gym or fitness provider', so whether it covers a yoga studio or a sole teacher needs checking (Queensland Government, last updated 23 July 2024). Victoria's guidance on fitness centre agreements, dated January 2011, says auto-renewal is unfair unless the student can opt out at sign-up, and that an early-cancellation fee must be a genuine pre-estimate of loss. It may be superseded, so check its currency (Consumer Affairs Victoria). For NSW, a 2015 news report said the government would cancel the Fitness Services (Pre-paid Fees) Act 2000. The report does not confirm that the change took effect, so do not treat it as settled. Check NSW Fair Trading before you sell prepaid packs in NSW.

instruction.heading: Guarantees, claims and pricing on value
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees apply to services and a 'no refunds' line does not override a student's rights for services (business.gov.au, Warranties and refunds, 27 May 2025). Publish only results you have measured, with consent, and check current ACCC guidance before publishing any measured claim. Price from the outcome and the risk, then check against cost and time. Public prices give the comparison. Central Yoga lists in-person single classes at $28, a five-class pack at $120 ($24 a class) and a ten-class pack at $220 ($22 a class) (Central Yoga, undated). ASMY lists a six-class pack at $80 valid for one month, a twelve-class pack at $150 valid for two months ($12.50 a class), and a twenty-class pack at $240 valid for three months ($12 a class) (ASMY, 6 November 2026). A pack gives a lower price per class, and its validity is part of what you sell, so state it. Show one clear total and say whether GST is included (WA Consumer Protection, updated 4 September 2026). For reformer Pilates, UniActive lists non-member casual reformer classes at $27, a five-class pack at $130 and a ten-class pack at $250 (UOW UniActive, undated). Average weekly reformer prices in one news report, citing an iSelect study that was not checked, ranged from $64 in Tasmania to $82.20 in Canberra (Concrete Playground, 24 November 2025).

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a student would repeat, using only things you can measure and control.
Set a time frame you can keep, and record how often you keep it.
List what the student must do, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a written plan, a timetable or a check-in.
Decide the make-up, pause and cancellation terms, and check that you can afford them.
Price from value, then check the rate against cost, time and insurance.

workedExamples.situation: A yoga teacher wants to sell a ten-class pack alongside casual classes. Students say they cannot tell whether a pack is worth it, and several want to pause for a holiday.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Set the pack price, its validity and the pause terms, and decide what the student must do to use them.
workedExamples.reasoning: Price the pack from your own per-class cost and the validity you can deliver, then compare it with public studio prices rather than copying them. Central Yoga's in-person ten-class pack is $220 and its single class is $28 (Central Yoga, undated). ASMY's twelve-class pack is valid for two months (ASMY, 6 November 2026). A pack that states its validity, a pause rule and a refund position in writing gives the student something checkable. If you take payment in advance, check the state rule first. Queensland limits prepayment to 12 months ahead, and the NSW position is unverified.

commonErrors.error: Making a guarantee you cannot afford to honour
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the guarantee to something you control, such as a make-up class.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate
commonErrors.prevention: Publish only results you have measured, with consent, and check current ACCC guidance first.

commonErrors.error: Selling packs with no written validity, pause or refund terms
commonErrors.prevention: State the validity, pause and refund position in writing before the first payment.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business and consumer guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. AUSactive sets registration criteria for yoga professionals, but this lesson does not treat them as a state licence. Whether a state requires registration for yoga or Pilates is not confirmed here.

Prepaid packs and cancellation rules differ by state. The NSW prepayment law is unverified: a 2015 news report announced its cancellation, and no source here confirms the outcome. Check NSW Fair Trading before relying on any NSW rule. Victoria's 2011 guidance may be superseded.

Pilates: the Pilates Association of Australia says its graduates need association membership to obtain combined liability cover, and says sessions should start with a health screening. These are association statements, not verified legal standards. Check your insurer's terms.
Health screening standards for yoga are not verified in this lesson. Do not promise health outcomes in any offer.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost, time and insurance.
Every pack and membership states its validity, pause rule and cancellation terms in writing before the first payment.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or pack terms with scope, exclusions, validity, pause and cancellation rules
Pricing check showing cost, hours, insurance and the decision made
summary: A good offer promises a measurable outcome you control, with a time frame, certainty and a fair cancellation rule.
Pause, prepayment and cancellation rules differ by state, and the NSW prepayment law is unverified here.
Higher rates follow from clearer value, not from longer hours.

officialReferences.title: Prepare quotes (business.gov.au)
officialReferences.covers: States that a written quote becomes binding once accepted and that a quote should recover cost plus a margin. Publisher: business.gov.au.

officialReferences.title: Warranties and refunds (business.gov.au)
officialReferences.covers: Says an optional written warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees, and that a 'no refunds' line does not override rights for services. Publisher: business.gov.au.

officialReferences.title: Estimates, quotes and deposits (WA Consumer Protection)
officialReferences.covers: Western Australia only. Asks for the total including GST and whether GST is included. Publisher: WA Consumer Protection.

officialReferences.title: Fitness Industry Code of Practice: cancelling a gym membership (WA Consumer Protection)
officialReferences.covers: Says the code covers yoga classes, and sets out cancellation by email, the 30-day effect of notice, and illness cancellation with a medical certificate. Does not say whether the code is mandatory. Publisher: WA Consumer Protection.

officialReferences.title: Join a gym or fitness provider (Queensland Government)
officialReferences.covers: Sets out prepayment limits of up to 12 months ahead, refunds within 14 days less services used, and a 48-hour cooling-off. Scope is 'gym or fitness provider'; coverage of yoga studios and sole teachers needs checking. Publisher: Queensland Government.

officialReferences.title: Preventing unfair terms in health and fitness centre membership agreements (Consumer Affairs Victoria)
officialReferences.covers: States that auto-renewal is unfair unless the consumer can opt out at sign-up, and that an early-cancellation fee must be a genuine pre-estimate of loss. Dated 2011; may be superseded. Publisher: Consumer Affairs Victoria.
